title: Vulva anatomy: external structures and blood supply
description: The external genitalia, carefully distinguished from the vagina: labia, clitoral complex, vestibule, openings, glands and perineum.

questions.question: What structures are included in the vulva?
questions.answer: The vulva includes the mons pubis, labia majora and minora, clitoral structures and vestibule with urethral and vaginal openings.

questions.question: Are the vulva and vagina the same thing?
questions.answer: No. The vulva names the external genital region; the vagina is the internal muscular canal extending toward the cervix.

questions.question: What are the labia majora?
questions.answer: Outer skin folds containing fat and connective tissue. Function: Protect the vestibule and inner folds.

questions.question: Where are the labia minora located?
questions.answer: Inner hairless folds, highly variable in size and pigmentation. Function: Border the vestibule and contribute to clitoral hood.

questions.question: What is the function of the greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands?
questions.answer: Function: Secrete mucus for lubrication. Paired glands posterolateral to vaginal opening; ducts empty in vestibule.
